Construct a canreg object

Source: R/as_canreg.R
as_canreg.Rd

This function constructs a canreg object, which contains cancer registry data, including incidence, mortality, and population information. Users can provide either a raw regi_data data frame containing inciden and deathda columns, or supply inci and mort data frames directly.

Usage

as_canreg(
  regi_data = NULL,
  inci = NULL,
  mort = NULL,
  pop = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  regicode = NULL,
  regicode_var = NULL
)

Arguments

regi_data

A data frame containing raw registry data with at least the columns:

  • inciden: date of diagnosis

  • deathda: date of death If provided, inci and mort will be automatically derived.

inci

A data frame containing incidence (case) data. If not provided, it can be derived from regi_data.

mort

A data frame containing mortality (death) data. If not provided, it can be derived from regi_data.

pop

A data frame containing population data. This is required.

year

Optional vector of four-digit calendar years or inclusive "YYYY-YYYY" periods. If specified, only cases or deaths from those calendar years will be included, for both raw and separate input tables. Incidence uses inciden and mortality uses deathda; missing event dates are excluded when filtering. Population rows are not filtered.

regicode

Character. A registry or area identifier for the data. It is stored as a character vector and is not limited to administrative division codes. Default is NULL.

regicode_var

Optional character string naming the column that identifies registries in all supplied data frames. When provided, the data are split by this column and one canreg object is created per registry. A single registry still returns a canreg; multiple registries return a named canregs object.

Value

A canreg object (S3 class canreg) or, when multiple registry codes are found with regicode_var, a named canregs object. Each canreg contains regicode, FBcases, SWcases, and POP.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Using raw registry data
canreg_obj <- as_canreg(
  regi_data = my_registry_df,
  pop = my_population_df,
  year = 2023,
  regicode = "410100"
)

# Build one canreg per registry using a grouping column
canregs_obj <- as_canreg(
  inci = incidence_df,
  mort = mortality_df,
  pop = population_df,
  regicode_var = "registry_id"
)

# Using separate incidence and mortality data frames
canreg_obj <- as_canreg(
  inci = my_incidence_df,
  mort = my_mortality_df,
  pop = my_population_df
)
} # }
